quote: We call it a grain of sand, / but it calls itself neither grain nor sand.
source: Wisława Szymborska, View with a Grain of Sand, lines 1 to 2, Ludzie na moście (1986) (trans. Stanisław Barańczak and Clare Cavanagh, 1995)

evidence.where: two independent reprints of the Barańczak and Cavanagh translation, read this run, agreeing verbatim on the first stanza and its punctuation; the printed volume itself was not opened
evidence.edition: View with a Grain of Sand: Selected Poems, Harcourt Brace, 1995; the same translation is reprinted in Poems New and Collected, 1998
evidence.locator: the opening two lines of the first stanza

reason: The proposal's own hedge can be dropped: both reprints print the comma after sand in line 1 and the stop after the second line, and both credit Barańczak and Cavanagh. This is Szymborska's third and last line of the year, after months 1 and 6, and she stands only once in October.
